title: Engineering Decision Table — The Measured Basis of a Baseline Reset under Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions
content:
# The Measured Basis of a Baseline Reset

Decision table for the basis the restated performance baseline of a subscription under Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions is measured from. A full year of readings is 12 to a point.

## Rule

- Where the subscription draws its data from the utility bills alone or from more than one source, the measured basis is the billed electricity gathered over the window.
- Where the subscription draws its data from its own meters or from the automation system and the interval readings posted in the twelve months ending on the day of the reset reach twelve for every point the subscription covers, the measured basis is the electricity those interval readings recorded.
- In every other case the measured basis is the baseline standing on the subscription, because the record carries no complete measured year to restate it from.

## Table

| Source the subscription draws its data from | Interval readings posted in the 12 months ending on the day of the reset | Measured basis |
|---|---|---|
| the utility bills alone, or more than one source | any | the billed electricity gathered over the window |
| the site's own meters, or the automation system | 12 or more for every metered point the subscription covers | the electricity those interval readings recorded |
| the site's own meters, or the automation system | fewer than that | the baseline standing on the subscription |

The reading test is a total: the interval readings posted in those twelve months must number at least twelve times the metered points the subscription covers.

## Boundary (hypothetical)

A subscription covering 12 metered points and drawing its data from its own meters needs at least 144 interval readings posted in the twelve months ending on the day of the reset. With 144 the electricity those readings recorded is the measured basis; with 143 the baseline standing on the subscription is.
